subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: After the `code_mode_exec` normalization blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept policy-active unified-exec routing plus fresh-thread rotation as the security boundary for Codex native PreToolUse enforcement?
rationale: The remaining choice changes Codex native execution routing and session continuity for policy-active users, and it depends on a Codex runtime behavior that OpenClaw cannot create by itself.

options.title: Fix Mapping Then Accept Scoped Route
options.body: Repair the Code Mode policy identity gap, keep the narrow positive-delivery approach, and require maintainer confirmation of the Codex runtime prerequisite before merge.

options.title: Prefer Fail-Closed Canary
options.body: Pause this PR in favor of #90805 if maintainers want missing native hook delivery to abort policy-active turns until upstream Codex behavior is fully proven.

options.title: Prefer Broad Native Surface Disablement
options.body: Use #90633 instead if maintainers prefer the stronger compatibility tradeoff of disabling Codex-owned native surfaces during OpenClaw policy enforcement.

recommendation.title: Fix Mapping Then Accept Scoped Route
recommendation.body: Repair the Code Mode policy identity gap, keep the narrow positive-delivery approach, and require maintainer confirmation of the Codex runtime prerequisite before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent adjacent ownership on the native relay fallback and CLI startup surfaces and is the best available decision owner for the compatibility/security tradeoff.
